We don't need to handle the single index in a special case. When it's an array both cases are treated the same. You can still loop on array of one item.
What about adding the ability to do some synchronize the parameters here?
I'm not sure about relying on a property that is somewhat internal. What about checking that search is called twice if you have two indices?
We can use a default value for the `indices` it will avoid the first path of the condition.

body: We can get rid of the second condition because we already throw an error when `indices` is not an array. If we move to the default value we can get rid of the complete condition. The value will always be there as an empty array.

By using the name of the index as key we can't have an autocomplete with the same index multiple times. Right now it's useless because we can't provide additional search parameters. But we can image to implement this functionality in the future. We have the issue with React InstantSearch, the idea was to require a `key` to avoid relying on the index name.
Why don't we use an empty array as default value? It means that we always need to check either the `results` or the `hits` in order to render. With a default value we can always loop on the hits.
Why don't we use `detach` instead? Otherwise the derived helpers are never cleaned up. The main instance will keep them for ever.
I guess a way to know if the search has been done is by using `widgets.indices[x].helper.search = jest.fn()` but it's still using `widget.indices` do you have any proposal?
Can you explain a bit more, I'm not sure to understand what you are meaning with "synchronize the parameters"
We have a key called `label` as well, I will switch the find using this key it will solve the issue 👍

I don't have a strong opinion on this one, for me in the end it's the same. For instance if you want to display a "no results" message you will have to do:

* `if (!index.hits) return ....`
* `if (index.hits.length === 0) return ...`

Your call :)

I did not know about the method `.detach()` and I did not know the main helper would keep a reference of the derived one, good call 👍
